# Quick Review



* __Language acquisition __ is the process by which humans acquire the ability to use\, produce\, and perceive language\!
  * FLA vs\. SLA
  * Learning vs\. acquiring
* How do children acquire language?
  * Induction AND innateness
  * Symbolization AND using tools
* What is baby talk?
* What are the stages of acquisition we discussed?

---




* We’ve talked about features of language this semester like “All languages change” and “All languages have rules\.”
* One other important feature about language:  __All languages are equally challenging__
  * …or equally easy\.
  * Every child who is capable of acquiring language will acquire a language
  * There is no biological basis that predisposes children to learn any PARTICULAR language \(This is usually determined by the language\(s\)/ culture\(s\) children grow up in\)
  * However\, acquiring certain features of certain languages may require more time to acquire
    * Ex\. German vs\. English definite articles


# Principles of Language Acquisition


---


# Activity time!



* In terms of adult input\, we’ve said that language acquisition isn’t merely imitation
  * But this does not diminish the importance of  _exposure_  to linguistic input
  * Acquisition REQUIRES interaction with speakers of the language being acquired
* Ex\. Genie \- [https://www\.youtube\.com/watch?v=mshp3s4r3u8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mshp3s4r3u8)
* We’ll watch the video\, and you can jot down things you notice about her language\, the research with her\, and anything else that stands out to you\.

---


![](images/Recitation%208_2.jpg)



* On the other hand\, parents do not TEACH language to their children directly
* What kinds of things DO parents teach children about how language works?
  * Talk to your neighbor and try to come up with some ideas
  * You can search the internet \(but try to find things LINGUISTS say\)
  * Or try to see what AI thinks\!
::: {.notes}

You can leave this out if you run out of time; I expect they’ll talk about manners, not cussing, and maybe some stuff about standard (e.g., “don’t say ‘like’ so much).

:::
